newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares erase losses, rise on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares erase losses, rise on foreign buying.

text.p: Strong buying by foreign institutional investors and local mutual funds wiped out early losses as share prices rose in afternoon trade on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Thursday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 4.08 points higher at 755.36 at 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
Brokers said they expected prices to continue rising.
"It seems that the market has now bottomed out and should recover further in coming sessions," said Sharat Jain of brokers V.K. Jain.
Traders said domestic financial institution Unit Trust of India, a seller in the early session, also made purchases at lower levels and helped lift prices.
Reliance Industries gained 3.00 rupees to 286.30 on institutional buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 1.45 rupees to 303.25 on foreign buying, they said.
Larsen and Toubro edged up 3.75 rupees to 207.75.
